text:
Jacob Trouba is on his fourth NHL team, and in San Jose he's the grown-up on a young blue line, playing 22 minutes a night, more than anyone would have predicted for a defenceman Evolving-Hockey rated below replacement level last season. The Sharks needed someone to take the hard minutes, and he takes them.

The production has been fine: ten points in 20 games, six of them in his last ten, roughly what our numbers expected. The defending is a split decision. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him stopping 16% of the entries aimed at him last season (typical 11%), which is the old Trouba, standing up at the line. The weak spot is what happens next: only 28% of his exits kept possession, so the puck goes off the glass and comes back. San Jose takes 46% of the expected goals at five on five with him on, a bit better than without him, on a team that gives up more chances than anyone. He's also one of the slowest skaters in the league by top speed, which makes those retreats harder. Watch his breakouts, not his hits.
